histology: glioblastoma, IDH-wildtype, WHO grade 4 (CNS WHO 2021); presenting tumor demonstrated intratumoral hemorrhage
stage: newly diagnosed; status post subtotal (partial) resection — gross-total resection NOT achieved; residual enhancing disease presumed on post-op MRI; no extracranial disease (GBM does not stage by AJCC TNM)

biomarkers.name: IDH1
biomarkers.decision_resolution: Tumor NGS and/or IDH1 R132H IHC. Confirms IDH-wildtype glioblastoma classification (CNS WHO 2021); excludes IDH-mutant astrocytoma/oligodendroglioma classification and the vorasidenib label (which is restricted to IDH-mutant grade 2 glioma).

biomarkers.name: CDKN2A (p16)
biomarkers.decision_resolution: Tumor NGS with copy-number calls, or FISH for 9p21 deletion. Decision relevance: CDKN2A/B homozygous deletion is a poor-prognosis molecular marker in glioma and is mechanistically linked to CDK4/6 inhibitor rationale (palbociclib, abemaciclib, ribociclib); co-occurs with MTAP loss on 9p21 and creates the PRMT5/MAT2A synthetic-lethal vulnerability.

biomarkers.name: MTAP
biomarkers.value: loss (homozygous deletion of 9p21, co-deleted with CDKN2A)
biomarkers.decision_resolution: MTAP IHC (loss of cytoplasmic staining) and/or NGS copy-number is the decision-grade resolution required by MTAP-selective PRMT5 inhibitor trials (e.g. AMG 193 / MRTX1719 / TNG908 / TNG462). Most current MTAP-loss-selective PRMT5 trial protocols require MTAP-null confirmation by an assay specified in the protocol.

biomarkers.name: MGMT promoter methylation
biomarkers.method: not yet performed (methylation-specific PCR or pyrosequencing required)
biomarkers.decision_resolution: MGMT promoter methylation by MSP, pyrosequencing, or methylation array. HIGH-PRIORITY DIAGNOSTIC GAP: methylation status dictates expected benefit from temozolomide (the standard-of-care backbone of Stupp regimen) — methylated tumors derive substantial TMZ benefit, unmethylated tumors derive minimal benefit and are candidates for TMZ-sparing or TMZ-alternative trial enrollment (e.g. TTFields-only after RT, or front-line trials).

biomarkers.name: EGFR
biomarkers.method: tumor NGS / FISH not yet reported
biomarkers.decision_resolution: Tumor NGS (amplification call) and EGFRvIII-specific testing (RT-PCR or NGS fusion call). EGFR amplification is present in ~40-50% of IDH-wildtype GBM; EGFRvIII opens enrollment into EGFRvIII-directed CAR-T and bispecific trials. Decision-relevant gap.

biomarkers.name: TERT promoter
biomarkers.decision_resolution: TERT promoter Sanger / NGS. Decision relevance: supports IDH-wildtype GBM classification per cIMPACT-NOW; not directly therapeutically actionable but part of complete molecular workup.

biomarkers.name: Chromosome 7 gain / chromosome 10 loss (+7/-10)
biomarkers.decision_resolution: NGS copy-number or FISH. Decision relevance: classification (supports molecular GBM diagnosis under cIMPACT-NOW Update 3 even without histologic grade 4 features).

biomarkers.name: BRAF V600E
biomarkers.decision_resolution: NGS or IHC (VE1). Rare in adult GBM but if positive opens dabrafenib + trametinib (tumor-agnostic label in BRAF V600E solid tumors when no satisfactory alternatives).

biomarkers.name: NTRK fusions
biomarkers.decision_resolution: RNA-based fusion NGS. Rare but actionable (larotrectinib / entrectinib tumor-agnostic label).

biomarkers.name: MMR / MSI
biomarkers.decision_resolution: IHC for MMR proteins (MLH1/MSH2/MSH6/PMS2) and/or NGS MSI call. Primary MMR-deficient GBM is uncommon; hypermutated GBM (often post-TMZ) opens pembrolizumab tumor-agnostic label and ICI trials.

prior_therapies.regimen: craniotomy with subtotal (partial) resection of the GBM mass; gross-total resection was not achieved; presenting tumor had intratumoral hemorrhage

targetable_features.feature: MTAP loss (homozygous 9p21 deletion, co-deleted with CDKN2A)
targetable_features.rationale: User-stated targetable feature. Mechanism: MTAP-null tumors accumulate the substrate MTA, which partially inhibits PRMT5; this creates a synthetic-lethal therapeutic window for MTAP-selective PRMT5 inhibitors (AMG 193 / MRTX1719 / TNG908 brain-penetrant / TNG462) and MAT2A inhibitors (AG-270 / IDE397). Multiple phase 1/2 trials are actively enrolling MTAP-deleted solid tumors, several with GBM-specific or CNS-penetrant arms. This is the single highest-yield molecularly targeted axis for this case.

User-stated targetable feature. Mechanism: loss of p16/INK4a derepresses CDK4/6 activity, providing rationale for CDK4/6 inhibitors (abemaciclib — CNS-penetrant and studied in GBM; palbociclib; ribociclib). Several GBM trials enroll on CDK4/6-pathway alteration including CDKN2A loss. Also a poor-prognostic marker that strengthens the case for aggressive combination strategies and trial enrollment over conservative monotherapy.

User-stated. A negative finding with decision consequences: IDH1-WT classifies the tumor as molecular glioblastoma under CNS WHO 2021, locks in the standard-of-care framework (maximal safe resection → Stupp: radiation + concurrent/adjuvant temozolomide ± TTFields), and excludes the IDH-mutant pathway therapies (vorasidenib, ivosidenib). Aligns trial eligibility toward GBM-specific trials rather than IDH-mutant glioma trials.

targetable_features.feature: Subtotal resection with residual measurable enhancing disease
targetable_features.rationale: Not a molecular target but a clinical-state feature that materially shapes the treatment plan: residual measurable disease (a) is independently prognostic for worse outcome, (b) enables response assessment on subsequent therapy (RANO criteria), and (c) makes the patient eligible for measurable-disease trial cohorts and for re-resection / laser interstitial thermal therapy (LITT) consideration at a high-volume neuro-oncology center.

Not a molecular target but a safety-relevant feature: prior intratumoral hemorrhage tightens the risk/benefit of bevacizumab (anti-VEGF; FDA-approved for recurrent GBM) and of any antiangiogenic or anticoagulant exposure. Should be carried forward as a safety annotation by downstream agents when scoring bevacizumab-containing or regorafenib-containing options.
